correctness.rationale: For arbitrary \(m\ge2\) the polynomial shear is an exact time-preserving conjugacy and direct multiplication proves \(J^3=0\). The planar Hamiltonian has exactly one oval annulus; the axial displacement integral gives an if-and-only-if closing condition. Even powers exclude all bounded forward solutions; odd powers have negative central drift and positive logarithmically divergent saddle drift, forcing a root. Analyticity and strict endpoint signs make the zero set finite. Every other planar orbit either leaves a bounded set or approaches a saddle/equilibrium with nonzero limiting axial velocity. The separatrix period logarithmic coefficient follows from V(v)=\(E_+\)-m(v-1)^2+O((v-1)^3), with a finite drift correction. The standalone checker adds reproducible tests but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The degree of the defining polynomial is a structural variable in an explicitly stated higher-degree open direction of the originating paper. The theorem supplies a sharp parity frontier between total absence and finite nonzero existence of all bounded/compact dynamics, for infinitely many natural degrees, and an explicit physical-time slowdown law. The statement remains valuable without a precise odd-degree count because it settles the recurrence-existence question and excludes hidden bounded recurrent states across the full three-dimensional phase space.
